title: SDK embedded sample-app roadmap and debugging cheats (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, copy-paste friendly onramp for engineers to embed Redwood SDKs into a sample app, plus a short roadmap and a debugging cheatsheet that devs and SEs can carry into demos. This is intentionally pragmatic — low ceremony, reproducible, and focused on the first hour to value.

Audience:
- Product engineers evaluating the API for an integration PoC
- Solutions engineers running customer demos and POCs
- Internal SDK maintainers who want canonical sample apps and troubleshooting guidance

Goals / success metrics (proposal):
- Time from repo clone -> working sample: <= 20 minutes (guided)
- Minimal friction: single-line install + 3 env vars to configure
- 80% of common errors covered in troubleshooting section
- 1 canonical sample per language (py, ts, go) plus a tiny backend-proxy example

High-level roadmap (next 3 sprints):
Sprint A (this sprint) - MVP sample and cheatsheet
- scaffold minimal Flask + Next.js examples (owner: Aisha, 3d)
- add README quickstart with copyable commands (owner: Marco, 1d)
- create short video (2–3 min) demoing local loop (owner: Tara, 4d)

Sprint B - polish & observability
- add telemetry examples (trace + token usage) and expected dashboard queries (owner: Ravi, 4d)
- add integration tests that run against staging API keys in CI (owner: Marco, 3d)

Sprint C - language parity and rollout
- add Go client sample + caching example (owner: Aisha, 5d)
- publish samples to learn.redwood.dev and include in SDK repo README (owner: Tara, 2d)

Mini-journeys (first-time dev flows) — keep them tiny and scriptable:
1) Quick local run (the 10-minute path)
- git clone <repo>
- cp .env.example .env && edit REDWOOD_API_KEY (or set env var)
- pip install -r requirements.txt OR npm install
- ./run-local.sh  # will start backend and open sample page
- Verify: type a prompt -> get streaming response within 2s

2) First commit (the 30-minute loop)
- follow quick local run
- make trivial change to UI, run unit test target (yarn test:ui)
- create feature branch and push to CI; ensure sample app passes smoke test against staging

3) SE demo / offline mode (demoing w/o live keys)
- run ./run-local.sh --mock to start a canned-responses mode
- use demo/fixtures/*.json prompts for consistent outputs

Quickstart (copyable commands for README) — keep this section near top of repo: 
- python (Flask) example: 
  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git
  2) cd sdk-samples/python-flask && cp .env.example .env && echo "REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx" >> .env
  3) pip install -r requirements.txt
  4) FLASK_ENV=development flask run --port=8080

- node (Next.js serverless) example: 
  1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git
  2) cd sdk-samples/nextjs && cp .env.local.example .env.local && export NEXT_PUBLIC_REDPW_KEY=sk-xxx
  3) npm install && npm run dev

Essential minimal config (opinionated):
- env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_MODEL (optional), REDWOOD_REGION
- single unified client wrapper in /lib/client.{js,py} that reads env and exposes 3 helpers: generate(), stream(), embed()
- keep example prompt sets in /demo/prompts with small README describing expected outputs

Debugging cheatsheet (most common issues and fast fixes):
- Issue: 401/invalid API key
  - Check env var name, no extra quotes, confirm key hasn't been rotated; run: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Issue: slow streaming responses in local dev
  - Confirm network egress to region (use ping/traceroute), ensure streaming port not blocked, test with small prompt to rule out tokenization overhead
- Issue: CORS errors in browser demo
  - Use local proxy (./run-local.sh --proxy) or configure allowed origins in dev routing; add dev-only header X-Dev-Debug to bypass strict checks
- Issue: model mismatch / unexpected output quality drift
  - Verify REDWOOD_MODEL set, check model version in response metadata, replay prompt against console to compare outputs, file an eval if regression seen
- Issue: huge token bill in CI runs
  - Add max_tokens cap on test prompt, enable a local stubserver in CI for smoke tests (see ci/stubserver.js)

Telemetry & validation (what to capture in samples):
- Instrument client to log: model, model_version, prompt_id (hash), token_count_request, token_count_response, latency_ms, region
- Provide a tiny dashboard query example (pseudo-sql) to compute median token cost per route and 95p latency

Checklists & release criteria for sample app PRs:
- README includes copy-paste quickstart and minimal troubleshooting FAQ (yes)
- CI smoke tests included and passing against staging keys (or stubserver)
- Small demo video recorded and uploaded to shared drive (2–3 min)
- License headers + security review (no secrets in repo)

Backlog / actionable TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Add CLI guided setup that prompts for API key + region and writes .env (owner: Marco, 2d)
- [ ] Create minimal TypeScript client example that uses streaming SDK (owner: Ravi, 3d)
- [ ] Add caching example (prefix + KV) and cost comparison note (owner: Aisha, 3d)
- [ ] Document rerouting/fallback behavior for Dedicated vs Hosted (owner: Tara, 2d)

Open questions (for product/rls):
- Do we want the sample apps to default to streaming or non-streaming? Streaming is nicer for demos but makes automated tests trickier. Proposal: streaming by default, with a --no-stream flag for CI.
- How opinionated should the client wrapper be about batching vs per-call? Suggest exposing both primitives and default to single-call for clarity in samples.

Notes for SEs (quick talking points):
- Use demo mode to ensure consistent outputs during customer meetings.
- Show token counter on demo page to explain cost tradeoffs when adjusting max_tokens/temperature.
- Highlight telemetry example that links tokens -> cost estimate in seconds (visual).

Next steps (this week):
- Marco: push MVP repo with Flask + Next.js + README (by Tue)
- Aisha: add caching + py client examples (by Thu)
- Ravi: prepare smoke CI with stubserver (by Fri)
- Tara: record demo video and upload (by Fri)

Quick links and snippets to stash into repo README for copy-paste:
- curl health check: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .
- local stubserver run: node ci/stubserver.js --port 5001

TODO: fold this cheatsheet into sdk-samples repo README and create a condensed 1-page PDF for sales playbooks.

Raw notes / ideas to potentially move later into separate docs:
- include a guided notebook that demonstrates embeddings + semantic search w/ small dataset (Jupyter + sample corpus)
- short section for private deployment customers: how to switch endpoint to private control plane + note about cert trust

Drafted by: Marco Chen (eng-developer-experience)
Comments: keep it iterative — this doc should be the low-friction source of truth for SEs and the sample app repo.
